text:
maya: @channel alert from infra-prober: sustained RT spike and 503s on /v1/generate in us-west-2, CPU on runtime nodes at 93% :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED - id=INC-2890 severity=high - paging eng-oncall
maya: I'm on it, pulling dashboard now. looks like traffic doubled and in-flight queues are building on runtime pools rdp-west-2-gpu-a
jordan: acked, grabbing logs and patient list. any customer-facing retries?
maya: yes, a few retries and some latency-sensitive customers seeing 5-10s tails, a couple of 503s. Dashboard shows max_in_flight configured 200 -> queue depth 180 -> timeouts firing
ashley: tagging customers with high QPS: acme-ads, quickchat, landing-embed-proxy. acme-ads has 12% error rate spike in last 5m
samir: can we shed non-critical routes first? e.g. /v1/embeddings and bulk/stream endpoints are heavy and not latency-critical
jordan: agree. propose temporary rate-limit: embeddings 40r/s global, and reduce per-tenant max_in_flight to 60 for default pool. also enable shedding of requests with "low_priority" header
maya: sound plan. ops-deploy-bot, can you push a traffic-control patch to the runtime config?
ops-deploy-bot: Received patch request. Preparing deploy to rdp-west-2-gpu-a. CI green. Rolling config change to 5% of hosts for canary.
maya: start canary then escalate if metrics look good. apply rate-limit and reduce max_in_flight on canary hosts first.
(5m passes)
jordan: canary hosts look stable: CPU down to 78%, queue depth halved, no additional 503s on canary
ashley: embedding QPS dropped as expected. acme-ads error rate decreased from 12% -> 3% on canary upstream
samir: ok ready to roll to 100% if no objections
maya: roll to 100%. ops-deploy-bot, rollout to remaining hosts.
ops-deploy-bot: Rollout started: patch id=tc-2890-01. Targeting 24 hosts, parallelism 4. Estimated finish ~8m
(6m passes)
jordan: metrics look good during rollout, overall CPU down to 64%, p95 latency improved from 1.9s -> 1.1s
maya: customer impact update: acme-ads errors back to baseline, QuickChat reports transient slow downs but no user-facing errors. Notified CS to watch for support tickets
ashley: small note: some internal batch jobs timed out due to lower max_in_flight, they are low-priority but kicked retry cascades in one queue. we should exclude batch-worker routes from shedding via header or route whitelist
samir: +1. we'll add route whitelist for /internal/batch* and increase timeout for those jobs to avoid retries. doing a quick patch now:
```json
{
  "traffic_control": {
    "default_max_in_flight": 60,
    "rate_limits": {
      "embedding": "40r/s"
    },
    "shedding": {
      "enabled": true,
      "priority_header": "x-req-priority",
      "whitelist_routes": ["/internal/batch"]
    }
  }
}
```
ops-deploy-bot: Whitelist patch deployed to 100% hosts, patch id=tc-2890-02
maya: good. monitoring: set temporary alert dampening for the embedding route to avoid noisy paging while we observe. also creating a short-lived dashboard for the runbook
jordan: I'm going to bump quota for acme-ads by 20% for 10m to clear their backlog — should we do it?
maya: yes, bump customer quota but do it on dedicated token only. don't change global rate limits. ashley, will CS coordinate with acme-ads?
ashley: messaging drafted and sending now: "We applied temporary traffic shaping to reduce latency; we've increased your quota momentarily to help clear in-flight requests. Monitoring closely."
samir: couple of follow-ups: 1) consider tuning request timeout: reduce global idle timeout from 45s -> 25s for public routes to fail faster and free resources; 2) implement adaptive max_in_flight: lower when CPU > 85%
jordan: for now keep timeout change manual; adaptive is longer term. we can reduce public timeout to 30s as a conservative step. anyone object?
maya: agree, set to 30s public timeout. ops-deploy-bot, apply timeout change to runtime config but exclude internal routes
ops-deploy-bot: Timeout change deployed: public_timeout=30s, internal routes unchanged. patch id=tc-2890-03
(3m)
maya: monitoring update: no further increases in error rate; overall system stable. we'll keep embedding rate-limit in place for 30m, then reassess
jordan: preparing incident summary for postmortem: root cause suspected traffic spike + a handful of oversized embedding requests causing KV cache pressure and starving generation pools. mitigation: rate-limit embeddings, lower max_in_flight, enable shedding, whitelist internal jobs, short timeout reduction, temporary per-customer quota bump
ashley: handing off to night on-call: @samir you're next, key watchpoints: p95 gen latency, queue depth, embedding error rate, acme-ads token backlog. contact list in runbook updated with commands
samir: thx. notes for next: auto-shed should be tuned to drop requests with x-req-priority=low after queue depth > 120, and consider adding a circuit-breaker that returns 429 quickly instead of waiting for timeouts
maya: handing off as primary for this incident to @samir. playback: all mitigations done, customer impact reduced to minor, runbook created, CS notified. escalation path: paged if error rate > 5% sustained for 5m
on-critical: ownerless batch jobs still retrying, we've created a ticket to fix later (TKT-4581)
samir: acked, I'll monitor the 30m window and update if anything changes.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED - id=INC-2890 status=monitoring owners=[samir]
maya: thanks everyone, nice quick coordination. leaving notes in incident tracker.
ashley: +1 great work :thumbsup:
samir: handing off to daily oncall at 2890012760 — keeping embeds rate-limit until then.
